title: sessionless-tool-delegation-proposal-wip
content:
Context:

This doc explores a low-friction design for enabling tool calling from the Hosted API without persistent session state on Redwood. The idea: clients can attach ephemeral assertions to single requests, delegating tool invocation responsibility to Redwood runtime and to registered connector backends, while avoiding long-lived session objects. Motivations: reduce server-side state, simplify private deployment requirements, make mobile/edge integrations simpler, and enable safe streaming tool handoffs.

Problem statement (short):
- Many customers want tool-calls that look like regular Hosted API calls but cannot or do not want to maintain session objects (cookie-like storage) in our control plane.
- Existing tool-call patterns assume a session + connector-reservation lifecycle that introduces complexity for transient clients (mobile, Lambda cold starts, edge workers).
- Need to support streaming partial outputs and structured tool responses (JSON) while preserving idempotency and safety.

Goals:
- Allow single-request tool delegation: client includes all info necessary for a tool call in the request (connector id, auth hint/token, intended side-effect metadata).
- Support streaming incremental responses while coordinating tool resolution and graceful fallbacks.
- Avoid or minimize server-side session state; ephemeral routing metadata only lived for the request duration.
- Provide safe defaults: sandboxing, redact sensitive outputs, audit logs for enterprise customers.
- Keep SDK ergonomics simple: one-call async/await patterns that optionally surface tool progress events.

Non-goals:
- Not replacing Dedicated/Private long-lived connector setups where customers want to manage connector lifecycle.
- Not handling multi-step tool transactions requiring cross-request consistency without explicit customer-managed tokens.

High level sketch of API surface (proposal):
- POST /v1/responses (existing) augmented with a new top-level field: "tool_delegation" (nullable).
- tool_delegation: {"connector": "connector-id", "auth": {"ephemeral_token": "..."}, "intent": "create-ticket", "safety_profile": "default", "call_mode": "sync|stream|fire_and_forget"}

Examples (request snippets):
- Non-streaming single-call:
  {
    "model": "rw-large-v1",
    "input": "create a bug for failing job 342",
    "tool_delegation": {
      "connector": "jira-cloud-01",
      "auth": {"ephemeral_token": "eyJ.."},
      "intent": "create-issue",
      "call_mode": "sync"
    }
  }

- Streaming response with progressive tool result frames (SSE or chunked JSON):
  client sets stream=true and call_mode=stream; runtime emits text deltas + special tool frames with type=tool.call/started, tool.call/progress, tool.call/result

Structured output contract:
- Tool frames use a compact envelope: {"frame_type": "tool_event", "event": "started|progress|result|error", "tool": "jira-cloud-01", "payload": "...", "schema_version": "v1"}
- result payload must include a minimal canonicalization: {"external_id": "JIRA-1234", "summary": "...", "status": "open"} when connector returns structured metadata. Free-form attachments allowed in attachments array but must be size-limited and redacted per policy.

Idempotency and retries:
- Because there is no session to dedupe, clients should supply an optional idempotency_key at request-level. Runtime will prefer that for dedupe (best-effort across short window ~5m).
- For streaming calls with call_mode=stream, tool progress frames include a monotonic progress token that allows resumption if client reconnects quickly; if idempotency_key present, runtime can reconcile final status.

Auth and privacy considerations:
- Ephemeral tokens are passed through by the client; runtime treats them as opaque and forwards to connector backend. Ephemeral tokens are not stored persistently by default in hosted mode.
- For enterprise Private deployments we will provide an option to inject customer-managed secret proxies so tokens never transit Redwood control plane. (see rollout)
- All tool outputs are subject to configured redaction and PII scanning. Default behavior: redact anything that matches high-confidence secrets regexes in tool outputs; enterprise can opt-in to full retention/audit.

SDK ergonomics (developer experience):
- JS SDK recommended surface: 
  - responses.create({model, input, toolDelegation, stream: false, idempotencyKey}) -> Promise<Response>
  - responses.createStream({..., onToolEvent: (evt) => {}, onDelta: (d) => {}}) -> AsyncIterator
  - convenience: responses.toolCall() wrapper that returns typed object if tool returns structured result
- Minimal escaping/hydration: SDK should surface tool_event frames as dedicated events, not blobbed into text; encourage structured parsing for reliability.
- Backcompat: existing SDK calls without tool_delegation maintain current semantics. If server receives tool_delegation but the model prompts do not call tools, runtime must still validate and either no-op or warn via telemetry.

Observability + telemetry:
- New telemetry fields to log per-request: tool_delegation.connector, call_mode, idempotency_key_present, ephemeral_auth_size_bytes, tool_frames_count, final_tool_status
- New dashboard tile: tool-delegation success rate, median wall-clock between tool.started -> tool.result, tooling-specific error categories (auth, rate limit, connector error).

Streaming behaviour and fallbacks:
- When call_mode=stream, runtime opens a connector call and streams back three kinds of frames in priority order: tokenized text deltas, tool_event frames, and meta frames (progress/audit). Clients should expect interleaving.
- If connector fails mid-stream, runtime will attempt fallback hierarchy: local stub (if available), alternate connector (if annotated), model-only fallback (synthesize apology + suggested next steps). All fallback events are annotated with reason codes for telemetry.

Rollout plan (phased):
1) internal alpha: expose endpoint behind a feature flag; limited to infra team and SEs. Connectors are mocked; security review for ephemeral tokens.
2) closed beta: integrate with a few stable connectors (jira, gmail, slack) via short-lived test credentials. Add SDK support and basic telemetry.
3) public beta: enable for hosted API customers by request; provide opt-out in account settings for token passthrough.

Compatibility notes:
- Private deployments: default is no-control-plane storage of tokens; we will document how to enable secret-proxying for enterprise.
- Dedicated customers with existing session-based connectors can continue to use session flows; sessionless is additive.

Open questions / tradeoffs (need decisions):
- How long should dedupe window be? (5m default) trade: longer helps retries but increases memory/coordination costs.
- Should runtime attempt syntactic verification of connector-specific payloads (e.g., ensure required fields for jira create-issue)? Pros: fewer runtime errors. Cons: couples runtime to connector schemas. Proposal: basic field presence checks for known connectors only; otherwise passthrough.
- Resumption semantics for streaming when client disconnects for >30s: can we support full resume vs best-effort? Proposal: support short resume (~10s) via progress token only; beyond that require client to re-issue with idempotency_key.
- Billing: tool-delegation calls may incur connector egress costs. Need pricing append to usage docs.

Security checklist (early):
- Threat model note: malicious ephemeral token leak, connector impersonation, replay attacks. Controls: short TTL tokens, enforce TLS, audit logs, optional customer-managed proxy.
- Redaction rules: apply post-tool-call PII scanning and mask before storing logs (hosted default).

Implementation notes (runtime):
- New request pipeline step: if tool_delegation present, validate connector id -> fetch connector routing info -> attach ephemeral auth header -> open connector stream (HTTP/2 or websockets) -> pipe events into response stream
- Use existing streaming mux layer but add a new frame type and wire in backpressure semantics for connectors (so slow connectors don’t stall text deltas indefinitely). Implement drop policies with annotated reasons.

Unresolved engineering TODOs:
- define connector registry schema (id, type, supported_schemas, failover_list)
- implement idempotency cache scope and eviction policy
- finalize schema for tool_event envelope (v1) and draft migration plan for v2

Next steps / action items (short):
- Product: finalize top-level UX decisions (dedupe window, default redaction policy) by 2025-03-20 (owner: Maya)
- Eng: spike on connector passthrough performance and backpressure strategy (owner: Ravi) 2w
- Security: run threat-modeling session and confirm proxy options (owner: Anya) 1w

Notes to self / scratchpad (informal):
- want this to be friendly to mobile builders: example snippet in react-native + minimal streaming handlers
- consider a tiny CLI debug tool to show interleaved frames for SEs
- slack thread: #product-hosted-api has initial signal from two customers wanting no-session flow (thread link in artifacts)

References and related work:
- previous drafts about resumable partial responses — see linked files in hosted-api folder (many)
- infra PR for streaming frame types (GH PR link above)

End of doc.
